en: My little brother ate my precious cake (and I was upset).
why: The adjective comes before its noun, を follows the noun, and the passive verb comes last before しまいました.

after: ので、{着替|きが}えました。
en: I got caught in the rain on the way home and my clothes got wet, so I changed.
why: {雨|あめ}に goes with {降|ふ}られて, then {服|ふく}が is the subject of ぬれて, and しまった comes before ので.

en: This book is read a lot by young people.
why: {若|わか}い describes {人|ひと}, に marks who reads it, and the passive verb goes before います.

before: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{隣|となり}の{人|ひと}に
en: On the train the person next to me stepped on my foot, and it hurt.
why: を follows {足|あし}, the passive verb takes を, and しまって comes after the て-form.

en: My mother made my brother eat vegetables he dislikes.
why: {嫌|きら}いな describes {野菜|やさい}, を follows it, and the causative verb stem goes before ました.

en: I want to let my children do what they like.
why: {好|す}きな describes こと, させて needs an object, and あげたい follows the て-form.

before: {社長|しゃちょう}は{部下|ぶか}を
en: I heard the company president kept his staff waiting for a whole hour.
why: も follows the amount {一時間|いちじかん}, then the causative て-form, then しまった.

en: Excuse me, could you let me rest a little?
why: {少|すこ}し comes before the verb, and ～させていただけませんか is a fixed polite request.

en: I once made my sister cry and got scolded by my mother.
why: {妹|いもうと}を needs {泣|な}かせて, {母|はは}に goes with the passive {叱|しか}られた, and ことが comes before あります.

en: When I was a child, my mother made me take piano lessons.
why: を follows ピアノ, then the causative-passive て-form, then いました.

en: At the drinking party I was made to drink alcohol I didn't want to drink.
why: {飲|の}みたくない describes お{酒|さけ}, を follows it, and the causative-passive verb comes last.

before: {昨日|きのう}は{先輩|せんぱい}に
en: Yesterday my senior made me carry heavy bags, and I got tired.
why: {重|おも}い describes {荷物|にもつ}, the object comes before {運|はこ}ばされて, and the result {疲|つか}れました comes last.

before: {子|こ}どものころは、{毎朝|まいあさ}{父|ちち}に
en: As a child, I hated being made to get up early by my father every morning.
why: {早|はや}く comes before the verb, の turns the verb into a noun, and が marks it before いやでした.

en: This is the watch my father gave me for my birthday.
why: に follows {誕生日|たんじょうび}, and the clause {父|ちち}が{誕生日|たんじょうび}にくれた describes {時計|とけい}.

en: The sweets I got from Tanaka-san were very tasty.
why: もらった describes お{菓子|かし}, は marks the topic, and とても goes right before おいしかった.

en: I plan to give my old computer to my little brother.
why: {古|ふる}い describes パソコン, を follows it, and あげる comes before つもり.

before: {道|みち}がわからなかったとき、{知|し}らない{人|ひと}が
en: When I didn't know the way, a stranger took me to the station.
why: まで follows {駅|えき}, {連|つ}れて{行|い}く is a set verb, and its て-form goes before くれました.

before: {日本人|にほんじん}の{友|とも}だちに
en: I had a Japanese friend look at my Japanese essay.
why: {日本語|にほんご}の describes {作文|さくぶん}, the object comes before {見|み}て, and もらいました follows the て-form.

before: {妹|いもうと}が{泣|な}いていたので、
en: My little sister was crying, so I sang her a song she likes.
why: {好|す}きな describes {歌|うた}, the object comes before {歌|うた}って, and あげました follows the て-form.

en: I forgot the lunch box my mother made for me.
why: {作|つく}ってくれた describes お{弁当|べんとう}, and を links it to {忘|わす}れて.

after: おかげで、すぐわかりました。
en: Thanks to the map my teacher drew for me, I found it right away.
why: {書|か}いていただいた describes {地図|ちず}, and の connects it to おかげで.

en: The president has already gone home.
why: お～になる is a fixed honorific pattern, and もう comes before it.

before: {先生|せんせい}は{明日|あした}{何時|なんじ}に
en: What time will the professor come to the university tomorrow?
why: へ marks the place before the verb, then ます, then the question marker か.

en: Shall I carry your bags for you?
why: お～する is a fixed humble pattern, and ましょう follows し.

en: I read the book my teacher wrote.
why: お{書|か}きになった is one honorific verb that describes {本|ほん}, and を links it to {拝見|はいけん}しました.

en: Manager, have you looked at these documents?
why: この comes before the noun, を follows it, and ご{覧|らん}に goes before なりましたか.

en: May I visit you at 3 p.m.?
why: そちらに marks the place for {伺|うかが}う, and ～てもよろしいですか is a set polite pattern.

before: {先生|せんせい}の{家|いえ}で、{奥|おく}さんが
en: At my teacher's house, I ate the food his wife made for us.
why: {作|つく}ってくださった describes {料理|りょうり}, and を links it to いただきました.

before: お{客様|きゃくさま}、こちらで
en: Please wait here for a moment, sir/madam.
why: {少々|しょうしょう} comes before the verb, and お{待|ま}ちくださいませ is a fixed polite phrase.

before: {会議|かいぎ}が{始|はじ}まる{前|まえ}に、
en: Please copy the documents before the meeting starts.
why: コピーして is one verb taking {資料|しりょう}を, and おいて goes before ください.

before: お{客|きゃく}さんが{来|く}る{前|まえ}に、
en: I chilled the beer before the guests came.
why: を follows ビール, then the て-form, then おきました.

en: Put the scissors you used back where they were, OK?
why: {元|もと}の describes {場所|ばしょ}, に marks where to put them, and おいて follows the て-form.

after: {駅|えき}に{聞|き}きに{行|い}きました。
en: I left my umbrella on the train, so I went to ask at the station.
why: {傘|かさ}を goes with {忘|わす}れて, しまった follows the て-form, and ので gives the reason.

en: I broke my mother's precious plate and got told off a lot.
why: {大切|たいせつ}な needs the noun {皿|さら}, then {割|わ}ってしまって, and とても goes before {怒|おこ}られました.

en: I left my wallet at home.
why: {家|いえ}に marks the place, {置|お}いてくる is one verb, and しまいました follows its て-form.

en: When I go to Japan, I want to try climbing Mt. Fuji.
why: に follows the mountain, {登|のぼ}って takes に, and みたい follows the て-form.

en: May I try this outfit on?
why: ～てみてもいいですか is a set pattern: て-form, みても, いい, です.

before: わからない{言葉|ことば}は
en: Try looking up words you don't know in a dictionary.
why: {辞書|じしょ}で marks the tool for {調|しら}べて, then みて, then ください.

en: I'm just about to make dinner now.
why: The object comes before {作|つく}る, and dictionary form + ところです means "about to".

en: I've just this moment arrived at the station.
why: {駅|えき}に goes with {着|つ}いた, and た-form + ところです means "just did".

before: {電話|でんわ}したとき、{兄|あに}は
en: When I called, my brother was in the middle of taking a bath.
why: お{風呂|ふろ}に goes with {入|はい}って, then いる, then ところ before でした.

en: The computer I bought just last week broke.
why: た-form + ばかり, then の links it to the noun パソコン.

before: {弟|おとうと}は{毎日|まいにち}
en: My brother does nothing but play games every day and doesn't study.
why: ばかり follows the noun ゲーム, then して, then いて.

en: I've only just come to Japan, so I don't have friends yet.
why: {来|き}たばかり is followed by なので, and まだ goes before the final clause.

en: Tanaka-san should be coming today, but he hasn't come yet.
why: {今日|きょう} comes before the verb, and dictionary form + はずです means "should".

en: I'm sure I put the key in my bag, but it's not there.
why: かばんの describes {中|なか}, に marks the place, and はず follows {入|い}れた.

before: あの{店|みせ}は{日曜日|にちようび}は
en: That shop should be closed on Sundays.
why: A noun takes の before はず, and です comes last.

after: ので、{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{行|い}きます。
en: It might rain tomorrow, so I'll take an umbrella.
why: {雨|あめ}が is the subject of {降|ふ}る, and かもしれない follows the verb.

en: Yamada-san may have already gone home.
why: {家|いえ}に goes with {帰|かえ}った, then かもしれません.

en: That story may be true, but I can't believe it.
why: かもしれません follows {本当|ほんとう}, and が joins it to the next clause.

before: {一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}
en: Even though I studied hard, I failed the exam.
why: のに follows the verb, then {試験|しけん}に goes with {落|お}ちて before しまいました.

en: Even though she promised, she didn't come.
why: のに attaches to した, then the subject, then {来|き}ませんでした.

en: Even though it's Sunday, I have to go to work.
why: な needs のに, {会社|かいしゃ}に goes with {行|い}く, and ～なければなりません is a set pattern.

en: My head hurts, so may I go home early?
why: ので follows {痛|いた}い, {早|はや}く comes before the verb, and ～てもいいですか is a set pattern.

en: It's quiet here, so it's easy to study.
why: A な-adjective needs な before ので, and the result comes after ので.

before: {日本|にほん}の{大学|だいがく}に
en: I'm saving money to get into a Japanese university.
why: ために follows the dictionary form {入|はい}る, then the object, then ためて.

pieces: {一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}
en: I'm working hard for my family.
why: の + ために, then the adverb before the verb, then います.

before: {試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}する
after: {勉強|べんきょう}しています。
en: I study until late at night to pass the exam.
why: ために follows する, and {夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまで is a set phrase in that order.

en: I'll make a note so that I don't forget.
why: ように follows the negative verb, メモして is one verb, and おきます follows it.

en: I practice every day so that I can speak Japanese.
why: {日本語|にほんご}が goes with the potential {話|はな}せる, then ように, then {毎日|まいにち} before the verb.

en: Please be careful not to catch a cold.
why: {風邪|かぜ}をひく is a set phrase, ように follows it, and {気|き}をつける comes next.

before: {最近|さいきん}、{漢字|かんじ}が{少|すこ}し
en: Recently I've become able to read some kanji.
why: {漢字|かんじ}が goes with the potential {読|よ}める, then ようになって, then きました.

en: I try to eat vegetables every day.
why: The object comes before {食|た}べる, and ようにしています is a set pattern.

en: I've decided to study abroad in Japan next year.
why: {日本|にほん}へ goes with {留学|りゅうがく}する, and dictionary form + ことにしました is a set pattern.

before: {来月|らいげつ}から{大阪|おおさか}の
en: It's been decided that I'll work at the Osaka branch from next month.
why: {大阪|おおさか}の describes {支店|してん}, で marks the place for {働|はたら}く, then ことになりました.

en: For my health, I make a point of running every morning.
why: {毎朝|まいあさ} comes before the verb, and ことにしています is a set pattern.

en: The meeting is set to be held next Monday.
why: {来週|らいしゅう}の describes {月曜日|げつようび}, に marks the day, and ことに follows the passive verb.

after: {今日|きょう}は{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
en: I drank too much last night, so I have a headache today.
why: すぎる joins to the verb stem {飲|の}み, and ので gives the reason.

en: This problem is too hard for me, so I can't understand it.
why: すぎて joins to the stem {難|むずか}し, and わかりません is the result.

en: I may have put too much salt in this dish.
why: {塩|しお}を goes with {入|い}れ, すぎた joins to the stem, and かもしれません comes last.

en: This pen is very easy to write with.
why: この needs a noun, とても comes before the adjective, and やすい joins to the stem {書|か}き.

before: {田中|たなか}さんの{説明|せつめい}は
en: Tanaka-san's explanation was a little hard to understand.
why: {少|すこ}し comes before the word, and にくい joins to the stem わかり.

en: These shoes are light and easy to walk in, so I like them.
why: くて links the two adjectives, やすい joins to the stem {歩|ある}き, and ので gives the reason.

en: Books with small print are hard to read, aren't they?
why: {字|じ}が{小|ちい}さい describes {本|ほん}, and にくい joins to the stem {読|よ}み.

before: {明日|あした}のパーティーに
after: 、あとで{連絡|れんらく}します。
en: I don't know if I can go to tomorrow's party, but I'll let you know later.
why: かどうか follows the verb, わかりません comes next, and が joins the next clause.

en: I'll ask the teacher whether this answer is right.
why: かどうか follows {正|ただ}しい, {先生|せんせい}に goes with {聞|き}いて, and みます follows the て-form.

en: Please check whether that shop is open today.
why: {今日|きょう} comes before the verb, {開|あ}いている is the て-form + いる, and かどうか follows it.

before: {昨日|きのう}、{泥棒|どろぼう}に
after: {警察|けいさつ}に{行|い}きました。
en: Yesterday a thief stole my bicycle, so I went to the police.
why: を follows {自転車|じてんしゃ}, the passive verb takes it, and ので gives the reason.

en: The manager helped me with my work, which was a big help.
why: The object comes before {手伝|てつだ}って, いただいて follows the て-form, and とても goes before {助|たす}かりました.

en: I'm tired, so I'll rest a bit before going home.
why: ちょっと comes before {休|やす}んで, てから joins the two actions, and {帰|かえ}る goes before ことにします.
